that says nothing.

platform, needed before anyone signs in, and it reveals nothing.

the platform keeps (§250). Null if they never signed in.

homeArea.description: The district they set as home, for offers (§186).

So the console can stop offering an action the server refuses (§118).

businesses.description: Where they work now. Removed memberships are history, and left out.

someone want it, in one line. The name above stays the short label.

instructions.description:
What to know before coming (§180): arrive early, bring a towel, park at
the back. Short on purpose — it is read on a phone, the day before.

A sale (§186): whole percent off every branch's price, 1–90. `null` ends
the sale; left out, it stays as it is.

The LAST day the sale runs, as a date (YYYY-MM-DD) in the platform's time
zone; it can be booked all of that day. `null`: until it is turned off.

offers.description:
Where this service is offered, and for how much at each branch (§72).

At least one: a service offered nowhere cannot be booked by anybody, and
creating one is almost always a mistake rather than an intention. A branch
can be removed later, which is the honest way to stop offering it there.

depositPercentage.description:
Share of the price the customer pays up front to hold the slot.

The lower bound is NOT expressed here: it is the live platform fee from
PlatformSetting, which an admin can change at runtime, so validating it
needs a database read and happens in ServicesService.

platformFeePercentage.description:
Two decimal places, as a STRING. A Decimal rendered to a float is the §55.2
mistake in a different place — and this is the number every booking's fee
is computed from.

providerCurrency.description: What the operator charges in. Equal to the above in a single-currency deployment.

exchangeRateUsdToProviderCurrency.description: Eight decimal places, as a string. Null when nothing is configured.

ageInHours.description: Null when there is no rate, or when no conversion happens at all.

conversionInUse.description:
Whether any conversion actually happens (§69.1).

False when the operator charges in the unit of account — the rate is then
pinned at 1 by §55.3 and cannot be wrong, so staleness does not apply.
Published rather than left for a client to infer by comparing two currency
codes, because a client that infers it wrongly shows an operator a red
"STALE" badge on a number with one legal value.

providerCurrency.description:
ISO 4217 code the provider charges in. "EUR" for MTN's sandbox.

Optional so a rate can be corrected without restating the currency; when
omitted the stored currency is kept.

exchangeRateUsdToProviderCurrency.description:
How many units of providerCurrency one USD buys.

Excluded minimum, not `@Min(0)`: a rate of exactly zero would convert every
deposit to nothing and charge customers zero, which is a worse failure than
refusing the value.

exchangeRateStalenessHours.description:
How many hours old the exchange rate may be before it is reported stale.

Zero is allowed and means "always warn" — legitimate for a currency moving
fast enough that any stored rate is suspect. Capped at a month, past which
the warning has stopped being a warning about anything.

note.description: What the number means, in words. Dates already set are never rewritten.

payoutHoldDays.description:
Days between an appointment resolving and its money becoming payable.

Zero is allowed and means "payable immediately" — a deliberate choice for a
platform that trusts its businesses, not an accident. Capped at 30: a hold
longer than a month stops being a settling window and starts being the
business financing the platform.

platformFeePercentage.description:
Percentage of the service price taken as the platform fee.

Two decimal places, matching the Decimal(5,2) column. Capped at 100 because
a fee above the whole price is nonsense, and every service's
depositPercentage must be at least this value — so raising it too far would
make existing services unsaveable.

exponent.description: Decimal places. Divide a minor-unit amount by 10^exponent to display it.

note.description: The rule in words, including the no-minor-unit case.

suggested.description:
A GUESS from the phone number, or null. Prefixes follow operators loosely
and a ported number keeps its old one, so a client should pre-select this
and still let the customer change it (§58.1).

choiceRequired.description: True when the number looks like one the platform cannot route on its own.

startTime.description:
Requested start, as an ISO-8601 instant (e.g. "2026-09-15T07:00:00.000Z").

Only the start is accepted. endTime is derived server-side from the
service's durationMinutes — letting a client send it would let them book a
15-minute slot for a 4-hour service.

quantity.description:
How many people (§136, §189). Left out, it is one — what every booking was.

Each person takes one of the branch's places, so the most is the places
the branch has; that is checked in the service, where the branch is
loaded. The 1000 here only bounds the type.

phoneNumber.description:
Payer's number in MSISDN form: digits only, country code first, no plus and
no spaces (e.g. "211920100200"). That is the shape MTN expects in
`payer.partyId`, and normalising here means the provider never has to guess
what a "+211 92 010 0200" was meant to be.

provider.description:
Which operator to collect through (§58.1).

Optional, and it WINS when supplied. The platform infers the operator from
the number's prefix, which is right most of the time and wrong for anyone
who has ported their number to another network — and a ported customer has
no other way to be paid from. So the inference is a default the caller can
always overrule, never a verdict.

What was actually sent to the operator. Both sides are returned so a client
never has to infer which currency a bare amount was in — in the sandbox
these differ on purpose (§52.1).

appointmentStatus.description:
The APPOINTMENT's status, not the payment's — the two are deliberately
separate fields because a failed payment leaves the appointment alive and
retryable, and a client that conflated them would cancel a held slot.

providerReferenceId.description:
Null once a payment has FAILED. The operator will not accept the same
reference twice, so clearing it is what makes a retry possible (§57.3) —
a client seeing null here should offer the payment again, not an error.

failureReason.description:
The operator's own words, for logs and support — NOT customer copy.

MoMo's four failure states collapse into one `FAILED` here (§57), and this
keeps what was lost: `FAILED: APPROVAL_REJECTED`, `FAILED: EXPIRED`,
`FAILED: INTERNAL_PROCESSING_ERROR` are all real values. A client must
translate before showing it to anyone, and should keep it visible somewhere
small, because it is what a support ticket needs.

reason.description:
Optional in the shape, REQUIRED when a business cancels — enforced in the
service, because only the service knows which side the caller is on.

A business cancellation costs the business money under §25, so it should be
a deliberate act with a stated reason. A customer cancelling their own
booking owes nobody an explanation.

gatewayChargeMinor.description:
What the payment gateway charged to process the refund, in MINOR UNITS OF
THE SETTLEMENT CURRENCY — the currency the provider actually charged in
(§45.4). REQUIRED when a business cancels an appointment whose deposit was
paid.

Supplied, never derived. The MoMo integration does not report its own
charge on a transaction or a refund (§36.2), so computing it from a
percentage constant would put a number in the ledger that the provider's
statement contradicts — and a ledger that cannot be reconciled is not
doing its job. Zero is allowed: sometimes there is no charge.

saved this" without a "you", and false renders a heart that cannot be
filled (§120.2).

center.description: Echoed back on a distance search, so a client can show what it searched.

endsOn.description: The last day it runs (YYYY-MM-DD, platform time), or null: until turned off.

listPriceMinor.description: One unit's price before the sale.

distanceKm.description: Only when a position was sent.

saved.description: Absent entirely for a signed-out reader.

priceMinor.description: This branch's price for one, as paid today: after the sale, if one is on (§186).

discount.description: The sale on today, or null (§186).

depositPercentage.description: A decimal string, like every percentage here (§128.20).

imageUrl.description: The cover photo (§132), or null — a client falls back to a category tile.

bookingCount.description: Paid, not-called-off bookings of this service at this branch (§135.1).

icon.description: An icon key or emoji. Never a URL.

otherLabel.description: What the business wrote when this kind is "Other" (§267) — show it in place of "Other".

kinds.description: Every kind of place it is, the main one first (§265).

average.description: Null when nothing has been reviewed. Not zero — zero is a rating.

saved.description: Absent entirely for a signed-out reader.

approxSettlement.description: Indicative only, and absent when no rate is configured (§66.2).

title.description: The headline under the photos on the service's page (§185).

instructions.description: What to know before coming (§180): shown before booking, and again on the reservation.

currency.description: The unit of account the price below is in.

depositPercentage.description: A decimal string, like every percentage here (§128.20).

priceMinor.description:
The price of ONE person as paid today — after the sale, if one is on
(§186). A booking for several costs this times how many (§136); how many
can come at once is the branch's `capacity` (§189).

discount.description: The sale on today, or null (§186).

images.description:
Photos of the service, cover first (§132). Empty is normal — a service
without photos is one nobody has photographed yet, not a broken one, and a
client should fall back to the shop's own picture rather than a gap.

dayOfWeek.description: 0 = Sunday, matching JavaScript rather than ISO (§12).

saved.description: Absent entirely for a signed-out reader.

capacity.description: Concurrent appointments this branch can run.

openNow.description: Computed against `timeZone`, not the reader's clock (§103).

coverImageUrl.description: The same picture the search card leads with (§133).

bookable.description:
Whether it can be booked right now. ONE field, not three: the branch
closing, the shop pausing and approval going are the same thing to a
customer (§120.1).

discount.description: The sale on today, or null (§186).

depositPercentage.description: A decimal string, like every percentage here (§128.20).

imageUrl.description: The cover photo (§132), or null — a client falls back to a category tile.

bookingCount.description: Paid, not-called-off bookings of this service at this branch (§135.1).

bookable.description:
False while the branch is closed, the business paused or not approved, or
the service paused at this branch — all temporary, all kept and marked
(§120). A service RETIRED by the business is not kept at all: see
`SavedServicePageDto.removed`.

removed.description:
How many saved services were found to be gone for good on this read —
retired by the business, or no longer sold at that branch at all — and
were taken off the list. Said once, so the customer knows why it is
shorter; zero the next time.

locationId.description: The branch it was saved at: the same service costs differently per branch.

label.description: What the phone called the place, e.g. "KG 11 Ave, Kimironko".

optedIn.description: True only after they turned it on themselves.

optedInAt.description: When they agreed; null when they have not.

district.description: Their district. Kept when they opt out, so opting back in is one tap.

spot.description: Their exact spot, if they gave one (§169). Measured from before the district.
An exact spot. Send `null` to forget it; leave it out to keep it (§169).

optedIn.description: Turning it on needs a district or a spot, here or already saved.

districtId.description: A live district. Send `null` to forget it.
